questions.explanation:
Verbal Aptitude → Vocabulary

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given: A sentence describing Indian students focusing intensely on their syllabus.
  • Find: The correct word to fill in the blank that completes the logical meaning of closing their minds to outside information.
  • Concepts used: Contextual Vocabulary, Prepositional Collocations.

Solution

  • The sentence establishes a contrast: students focus heavily on the syllabus and studying for tests, meaning they ignore things that are not part of the exam requirements.
  • We need an adjective that means "irrelevant" or "unrelated" and pairs correctly with the preposition "to".
  • "Extraneous" means irrelevant or unrelated to the subject being dealt with. The phrase "extraneous to" is grammatically sound.
  • "Outside" is incorrect because it does not idiomatically pair with "to" in this context (it would simply be "outside the requirements").
  • "Related" and "useful" contradict the logical flow of "closing their minds" to non-syllabus items.

Final Answer

Answer: extraneous, Correct option: 2 (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | GA Q5
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: A function f(x) is linear and has a value of 29 at \(x = -2\) and 39 at \(x = 3\). Find its value at \(x = 5\).
questions.explanation:
Quantitative Aptitude → Numerical Computation and Estimation

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given: A linear function \(f(x)\) where \(f(-2) = 29\) and \(f(3) = 39\)
  • Find: The value of \(f(5)\)
  • Concepts used: Equation of a Straight Line, Interpolation/Extrapolation.

Solution

A linear function can be represented as \(f(x) = mx + c\), where \(m\) is the constant slope.

Calculate the slope \(m\) using the two given points \((-2,\, 29)\) and \((3,\, 39)\):

\[m = \frac{f(x_2) - f(x_1)}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{39 - 29}{3 - (-2)} = \frac{10}{5} = 2 \]

With \(m = 2\), apply the slope-point form to extrapolate to \(x = 5\):

\[f(5) = f(3) + m(5 - 3) = 39 + 2(2) = 39 + 4 = 43 \]

Final Answer

Answer: 43, Correct option: 3 (C)

  • Find: The correct equation from the options.
  • Concepts used: Piecewise Functions, Absolute Value Operations, Graph Matching.

Solution

Analyze the geometric behavior of Option (B): \(x = -(y - |y|)\)

Final Answer

Answer: \(x = -(y - |y|)\), Correct option: 2 (B)

The head of a newly formed government desires to appoint five of the six selected members P, Q, R, S, T, and U to portfolios of Home, Power, Defense, Telecom, and Finance. U does not want any portfolio if S gets one of the five. R wants either Home or Finance or no portfolio. Q says that if S gets either Power or Telecom, then she must get the other one. T insists on a portfolio if P gets one.

Which is the valid distribution of portfolios?
questions.explanation:
Analytical Aptitude → Logic

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given: Six members (P, Q, R, S, T, U) and five portfolios (Home, Power, Defense, Telecom, Finance). One person will get no portfolio.
  • Rules:
    1. If S gets a portfolio → U gets none.
    2. R wants Home, Finance, or None.
    3. If S gets Power or Telecom → Q must get the other (Telecom or Power respectively).
    4. If P gets a portfolio → T must get a portfolio.
  • Find: The valid distribution of portfolios.
  • Concepts used: Rule-based Elimination, Logical Constraints.

Solution

  • Test (A): R gets Defense. This violates Rule 2 (R wants Home, Finance, or none). ✗
  • Test (C): S gets Telecom. By Rule 1, U must get no portfolio. However, U gets Finance. This violates Rule 1. ✗

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q11
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
For what value of \(p\) the following set of equations will have no solution?

\[2x + 3y = 5 \]
\[3x + py = 10 \]
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra / System of Linear Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: System of equations:
    \[2x + 3y = 5 \]\[3x + py = 10 \]
  • Aim: Find the value of \(p\) for which the system will have no solution.

3. Core Concepts:

For a system of two linear equations \(a_1x + b_1y = c_1\) and \(a_2x + b_2y = c_2\), the system has no solution (parallel, non-coincident lines) when: \[ rac{a_1}{a_2} = rac{b_1}{b_2} eq rac{c_1}{c_2} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Extract coefficients from both equations.
  2. Apply the no-solution condition to set up an equation for \(p\).
  3. Solve for \(p\) using the equality part.
  4. Verify the inequality condition holds for the calculated \(p\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify coefficients:
    \(a_1 = 2,\; b_1 = 3,\; c_1 = 5\)
    \(a_2 = 3,\; b_2 = p,\; c_2 = 10\)
  2. Apply condition for parallel non-coincident lines:
    \[ rac{2}{3} = rac{3}{p} eq rac{5}{10} \]
  3. Solve for \(p\):
    \[ rac{2}{3} = rac{3}{p} \implies 2p = 9 \implies p = 4.5 \]
  4. Verify inequality:
    \(\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{5}{10} = 0.5\) and \(\dfrac{b_1}{b_2} = \dfrac{3}{4.5} \approx 0.667\)
    Since \(0.667 eq 0.5\), the lines are parallel but not coincident. ✓

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.5  |  Accepted key range: 4.49 to 4.51

questions.question: The integral \(\int_{x_1}^{x_2} x^2 dx\) with \(x_2 > x_1 > 0\) is evaluated analytically as well as numerically using a single application of the trapezoidal rule. If \(I\) is the exact value of the integral obtained analytically and \(J\) is the approximate value obtained using the trapezoidal rule, which of the following statements is correct about their relationship?
options: Insufficient data to determine the relationship

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Insufficient data to determine the relationship
structuredOptions.html: Insufficient data to determine the relationship

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods / Numerical Integration

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Integral: \(\displaystyle\int_{x_1}^{x_2} x^2\,dx\) with \(x_2 > x_1 > 0\)
    • Analytical (exact) value \(= I\)
    • Numerical value using a single application of the trapezoidal rule \(= J\)
  • Aim: Determine the correct mathematical relationship between \(I\) and \(J\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Analytical Integration (\(I\)): Yields the exact area under the curve \(f(x)\).
  • Trapezoidal Rule (\(J\)): Approximates the area by a straight secant line between \((x_1, f(x_1))\) and \((x_2, f(x_2))\).
  • Error via Concavity: If \(f''(x) > 0\) everywhere, the function is strictly convex (concave upward). A secant line between two points on a convex curve lies entirely above the curve, so the trapezoid overestimates the exact area.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify \(f(x) = x^2\) and compute \(f''(x)\).
  2. Determine concavity over the interval.
  3. Conclude the geometric relationship between \(J\) and \(I\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compute derivatives:
    \(f(x) = x^2,\quad f'(x) = 2x,\quad f''(x) = 2\)
  2. Analyze concavity:
    Since \(f''(x) = 2 > 0\) globally, the curve \(y = x^2\) is strictly convex (concave upward) between any \(x_1\) and \(x_2\).
  3. Compare areas:
    The straight line forming the top of the trapezoid lies strictly above the parabola \(y = x^2\). Therefore the trapezoidal area overestimates the true area: \(J > I\).

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q13
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Consider the following probability mass function (p.m.f.) of a random variable X:

\[p(x,q) = \begin{cases} q & \text{if } X = 0 \\ 1 - q & \text{if } X = 1 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

If \(q = 0.4\), the variance of X is __________.
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability and Statistics / Probability Distributions

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Probability Mass Function (PMF):
    \(p(x,q) = q\) for \(x = 0\)
    \(p(x,q) = 1-q\) for \(x = 1\)
    \(p(x,q) = 0\) otherwise
    Parameter \(q = 0.4\)
  • Aim: Calculate the variance of the random variable \(X\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Expected Value (Mean): \(E[X] = \sum[x \cdot P(X=x)]\)
  • Expected Value of \(X^2\): \(E[X^2] = \sum[x^2 \cdot P(X=x)]\)
  • Variance: \(\text{Var}(X) = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2\)
  • Distribution Recognition: This defines a Bernoulli distribution. Variance \(= p(1-p)\) where \(p = P(X=1)\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Substitute \(q = 0.4\) to find numerical probabilities.
  2. Calculate \(E[X]\) and \(E[X^2]\).
  3. Apply the variance formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Determine probabilities:
    \(P(X=0) = q = 0.4\)
    \(P(X=1) = 1-q = 0.6\)
  2. Calculate \(E[X]\):
    \[ E[X] = (0 \times 0.4) + (1 \times 0.6) = 0.6 \]
  3. Calculate \(E[X^2]\):
    \[ E[X^2] = (0^2 \times 0.4) + (1^2 \times 0.6) = 0.6 \]
  4. Calculate Variance:
    \[\text{Var}(X) = 0.6 - (0.6)^2 = 0.6 - 0.36 = 0.24 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.24  |  Accepted key range: 0.23 to 0.25

questions.question:
Workability of concrete can be measured using slump, compaction factor and Vebe time. Consider the following statements for workability of concrete:

(i) As the slump increases, the Vebe time increases
(ii) As the slump increases, the compaction factor increases

Which of the following is TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Construction Materials | Concrete Technology / Properties of Fresh Concrete

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Two statements:
    (i) As the slump increases, the Vebe time increases.
    (ii) As the slump increases, the compaction factor increases.
  • Aim: Identify which statements are TRUE.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Slump Test: Higher slump values directly indicate higher workability (fluidity).
  • Vebe Time Test: Measures time to remold a concrete cone under vibration. High workability → concrete remolds rapidly → lower Vebe time.
  • Compaction Factor Test: Ratio of partially compacted to fully compacted concrete weight. High workability → easy self-compaction under gravity → higher compaction factor (closer to 1.0).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Connect increasing slump to increasing workability.
  2. Evaluate statement (i) by correlating high workability to Vebe time behavior.
  3. Evaluate statement (ii) by correlating high workability to compaction factor behavior.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Evaluate Statement (i):
    Increased slump \(\implies\) Increased workability \(\implies\) Less time to remold \(\implies\) Vebe time decreases.
    Conclusion: Statement (i) is False.
  2. Evaluate Statement (ii):
    Increased slump \(\implies\) Higher workability \(\implies\) Better self-compaction \(\implies\) Compaction factor increases.
    Conclusion: Statement (ii) is True.

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q15

questions.question:
Consider the following statements for air-entrained concrete:

(i) Air-entrainment reduces the water demand for a given level of workability
(ii) Use of air-entrained concrete is required in environments where cyclic freezing and thawing is expected

Which of the following is TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Construction Materials | Concrete Technology / Chemical Admixtures

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Two statements regarding air-entrained concrete:
    (i) Air-entrainment reduces the water demand for a given level of workability.
    (ii) Use of air-entrained concrete is required in environments where cyclic freezing and thawing is expected.
  • Aim: Determine the validity of both statements.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Rheological Effect (Statement i): Microscopic air bubbles act like flexible "ball bearings," reducing internal friction between aggregate particles and enhancing workability. For a given target slump, an air-entrained mix requires less mixing water than a non-entrained mix.
  • Durability Effect (Statement ii): In cold climates, capillary water inside hardened concrete expands ~9% upon freezing, generating destructive tensile stresses. Entrained air voids act as relief chambers for expanding ice. This is a mandatory code requirement (e.g., ACI 318, IS 456) for freeze-thaw exposure.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Validate statement (i) through the physical lubrication mechanism in fresh concrete.
  2. Validate statement (ii) through the expansion-relief mechanism in hardened concrete.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Statement (i): Air voids improve flowability, so the designer can decrease the water-cement ratio while maintaining the desired slump. Water demand is reduced.
    Conclusion: Statement (i) is True.
  2. Statement (ii): Entrained air prevents spalling and scaling from ice expansion. It is universally required for cyclic freeze-thaw exposure.
    Conclusion: Statement (ii) is True.

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (A)

  • Stiffness Coefficient Definition: \(K_{ij}\) = the force required at DOF \(i\) to induce a unit displacement at DOF \(j\), while all other DOFs are held at zero.
  • For \(K_{22}\): Apply transverse unit displacement (\(\Delta = 1\)) at DOF 2, while restraining rotation at DOF 3 (\(\theta = 0\)) and axial movement at DOF 1.
  • This mimics a beam with both ends fixed against rotation, subject to a relative transverse displacement.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Define physical constraints for extracting \(K_{22}\).
  2. Apply standard structural mechanics formula for end-shear in a beam subjected to relative end settlement with no rotation.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Physical boundaries:
    Apply \(\Delta = 1\) transversely at the right end, maintain \(\theta = 0\) at both ends (left end is fixed natively).
  2. Standard shear force relationship:
    The shear force \(V\) in a beam of length \(L\) and flexural rigidity \(EI\) with both ends fixed against rotation under relative displacement \(\Delta\) is: \[V = \frac{12EI}{L^3}\Delta \]
  3. Substitute unit displacement:
    \[K_{22} = \frac{12EI}{L^3}(1) = \frac{12EI}{L^3} \]

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (B)

questions.question: The development length of a deformed reinforcement bar can be expressed as \((1/k) (\phi\sigma_s/\tau_{bd})\). From the IS:456-2000, the value of \(k\) can be calculated as __________.
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Structures | Working Stress & Limit State Design / Bond & Development Length

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data: General formula for development length of a deformed bar: \[L_d = \frac{1}{k}\left(\frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{\tau_{bd}}\right) \]
  • Aim: Calculate the dimensionless constant \(k\) as per IS 456:2000.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Base Formula (IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.2.1): \[L_d = \frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{4\,\tau_{bd}} \] where \(\tau_{bd}\) is the design bond stress for plain bars in tension.
  • Deformed Bar Modifier (Cl. 26.2.1.1): For deformed bars conforming to IS 1786, the tabulated \(\tau_{bd}\) values are increased by 60% (multiplied by \(1.6\)).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Start with the base development length formula.
  2. Apply the 60% increase modifier for deformed bars.
  3. Rearrange to match the provided formula and extract \(k\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Base formula:
    \[L_d = \frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{4\,\tau_{bd,\text{actual}}} \]
  2. Express actual bond stress for deformed bars:
    \[\tau_{bd,\text{actual}} = 1.6 \times \tau_{bd} \]
  3. Substitute and simplify:
    \[L_d = \frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{4 \times 1.6\,\tau_{bd}} = \frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{6.4\,\tau_{bd}} = \frac{1}{6.4}\left(\frac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{\tau_{bd}}\right) \]
  4. Extract \(k\):
    Comparing with the given formula \(L_d = \dfrac{1}{k}\left(\dfrac{\phi\,\sigma_s}{\tau_{bd}}\right)\): \[k = 6.4 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 6.4  |  Accepted key range: 6.38 to 6.42

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q19
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: For the beam shown below, the value of the support moment \(M\) is __________ kN-m.
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Indeterminate Structures (Beams)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Symmetric continuous beam with an internal hinge at the center
    • Total length = 8 m
    • Supports: Fixed at both ends (A and E), roller supports at 3 m from each end (B and D)
    • Internal hinge (C) at the center (4 m from each end)
    • Point load at internal hinge: \(P = 20\text{ kN}\) (downward)
    • Flexural rigidity \(EI\) is constant throughout
  • Aim: Determine the support moment \(M\) at the left fixed support.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Symmetry: The internal hinge at the center transmits no bending moment (\(M_C = 0\)). The 20 kN load is shared equally → 10 kN to each half.
  • Overhang Effect: The 10 kN downward shear at C induces a hogging moment at B.
  • Conjugate Beam Method: Since A is a fixed support (\(\theta_A = 0\)) and B is a non-yielding roller (\(y_B = 0\)), the tangential deviation of B from A is zero. This provides the compatibility condition.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Isolate the left half (Span AC): fixed at A, roller at B (3 m from A), overhang BC (1 m).
  2. Apply 10 kN downward shear at free end C.
  3. Calculate bending moment at B from the overhang.
  4. Use the conjugate beam method on span AB to find the fixed-end moment at A.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Overhang Moment at B:
    \[M_B = -(10\text{ kN}) \times (1\text{ m}) = -10\text{ kNm (Hogging)} \]
  2. Conjugate Beam for Span AB (length \(L = 3\text{ m}\)):
    In the conjugate beam, A (fixed) becomes a free end and B (roller) becomes a simple support. For equilibrium of the conjugate beam, the moment of the \(M/EI\) diagram about B must be zero (i.e., tangential deviation \(t_{B/A} = 0\)).
  3. Moment of \(M/EI\) diagram about B:
    The BMD on AB is a trapezoid formed by \(M_A\) and \(M_B\):
    • Area due to \(M_A\): \(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times M_A\), centroid at \(\dfrac{2}{3} \times 3 = 2\text{ m}\) from B
    • Area due to \(M_B\): \(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times M_B\), centroid at \(\dfrac{1}{3} \times 3 = 1\text{ m}\) from B
    \[\sum M_{\text{about B}} = 0 \implies \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times M_A \times 2\right) + \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times M_B \times 1\right) = 0 \]\[3M_A + 1.5M_B = 0 \]
    Substituting \(M_B = -10\text{ kNm}\):
    \[3M_A + 1.5(-10) = 0 \implies 3M_A = 15 \implies M_A = +5\text{ kNm} \]
  4. Sign Convention:
    A positive result indicates a sagging (counter-clockwise reaction) moment at A with magnitude 5 kNm.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 5 kNm  |  Accepted key range: 5 to 5

questions.question: Two triangular wedges are glued together as shown in the following figure. The stress acting normal to the interface, \(\sigma_n\) is __________ MPa.
questions.explanation:

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Square block split by a diagonal interface at \(45^\circ\)
    • Horizontal stress on vertical faces: \(\sigma_x = 100\text{ MPa}\) (Tensile)
    • Vertical stress on horizontal faces: \(\sigma_y = 100\text{ MPa}\) (Compressive)
    • Shear stress: \(\tau_{xy} = 0\)
  • Aim: Find the stress acting normal to the glued interface (\(\sigma_n\)).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Sign Convention: Tensile stress is positive (\(+\)), Compressive stress is negative (\(-\)).
  • Stress Transformation: Normal stress on an inclined plane whose normal makes angle \(\theta\) with positive x-axis: \[\sigma_n = \frac{\sigma_x + \sigma_y}{2} + \frac{\sigma_x - \sigma_y}{2}\cos(2\theta) + \tau_{xy}\sin(2\theta) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Extract stress components with proper signs.
  2. Determine the angle of the normal to the \(45^\circ\) interface.
  3. Substitute into the stress transformation equation.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify Stresses:
    \[\sigma_x = +100\text{ MPa}, \quad \sigma_y = -100\text{ MPa}, \quad \tau_{xy} = 0 \]
  2. Identify Plane Angle:
    The interface is inclined at \(45^\circ\) to the horizontal. The normal to this interface makes \(\theta = 135^\circ\) with the positive x-axis. Thus \(2\theta = 270^\circ\).
  3. Calculate Normal Stress:
    \[\sigma_n = \frac{100 + (-100)}{2} + \frac{100 - (-100)}{2}\cos(270^\circ) + 0 \]\[\sigma_n = 0 + 100 \times (0) = 0\text{ MPa} \]
    Note: This plane represents the plane of maximum shear stress in a state of pure shear, where normal stress is strictly zero.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0 MPa  |  Accepted key range: 0 to 0

questions.question: A fine-grained soil has 60% (by weight) silt content. The soil behaves as semi-solid when water content is between 15% and 28%. The soil behaves fluid-like when the water content is more than 40%. The ‘Activity’ of the soil is

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Application
  • Given Data:
    • Soil type: Fine-grained
    • Silt content = 60% (by weight)
    • Semi-solid state water content range = 15% to 28%
    • Fluid-like state water content > 40%
  • Aim: Calculate the Activity of the soil.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Atterberg Limits:
    • Plastic Limit (\(w_P\)): Boundary between semi-solid and plastic states
    • Liquid Limit (\(w_L\)): Boundary between plastic and liquid (fluid-like) states
  • Plasticity Index: \(I_P = w_L - w_P\)
  • Activity of Soil: \[A = \frac{I_P}{\%\text{ Clay fraction}} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify \(w_P\) and \(w_L\) from the given state boundaries.
  2. Calculate Plasticity Index (\(I_P\)).
  3. Determine clay content fraction.
  4. Calculate Activity.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify Limits:
    Semi-solid range ends at 28% → \(w_P = 28\%\)
    Fluid-like state starts at 40% → \(w_L = 40\%\)
  2. Calculate \(I_P\):
    \[I_P = 40\% - 28\% = 12\% \]
  3. Determine Clay Fraction:
    Fine-grained soil consists of silt and clay:
    \[\%\text{ Clay} = 100\% - 60\%\text{ (Silt)} = 40\% \]
  4. Calculate Activity:
    \[A = \frac{12}{40} = 0.30 \]

Correct option: (C)

questions.question: In an unconsolidated undrained triaxial test, it is observed that an increase in cell pressure from 150 kPa to 250 kPa leads to a pore pressure increase of 80 kPa. It is further observed that, an increase of 50 kPa in deviatoric stress results in an increase of 25 kPa in the pore pressure. The value of Skempton’s pore pressure parameter B is:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Unconsolidated Undrained (UU) triaxial test:
    StageApplied Stress IncrementPore Pressure Increase
    Stage 1 (Cell pressure)\(\Delta\sigma_3 = 250 - 150 = 100\text{ kPa}\)\(\Delta u_c = 80\text{ kPa}\)
    Stage 2 (Shearing)\(\Delta\sigma_d = 50\text{ kPa}\)\(\Delta u_d = 25\text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Calculate Skempton's pore pressure parameter \(B\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Skempton's Pore Pressure Equation: \[ \Delta u = B\left[\Delta\sigma_3 + A(\Delta\sigma_1 - \Delta\sigma_3)\right] \]
  • Cell Pressure Stage (deviatoric stress = 0): simplifies to \(\Delta u_c = B\,\Delta\sigma_3\)
  • Shearing Stage (cell pressure constant): simplifies to \(\Delta u_d = B \cdot A \cdot \Delta\sigma_d\)

4. Solution Method:

Since only parameter \(B\) is required, use only Stage 1 data.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Isolate relevant equation:
    \[\Delta u_c = B\,\Delta\sigma_3 \]
  2. Substitute values:
    \[80\text{ kPa} = B \times 100\text{ kPa} \]
  3. Calculate B:

3. Core Concepts:

  • Contractive/Dilative Behavior: Loose sands contract (decrease in volume) on shearing. Dense sands dilate (increase in volume). Under undrained conditions, dilation causes negative pore pressures.
  • Expansive Soils: Soils rich in montmorillonite (e.g., Black cotton soil) exhibit severe volume changes (swelling/shrinkage) upon wetting/drying.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: In a two-dimensional steady flow field, in a certain region of the x-y plane, the velocity component in the x-direction is given by \(v_x = x^2\) and the density varies as \(\rho = \frac{1}{x}\). Which of the following is a valid expression for the velocity component in the y-direction, \(v_y\)?
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Kinematics of Fluid Flow

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Two-dimensional steady flow field
    • Velocity in x-direction: \(v_x = x^2\)
    • Density variation: \(\rho = \dfrac{1}{x}\)
  • Aim: Find a valid expression for the y-direction velocity component (\(v_y\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Continuity Equation for Compressible, Steady Flow: For steady 2D flow, conservation of mass requires: \[\frac{\partial(\rho v_x)}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial(\rho v_y)}{\partial y} = 0 \] Since density \(\rho\) is not constant, it cannot be canceled out.

4. Solution Method:

Substitute given expressions for \(\rho\) and \(v_x\), evaluate the partial derivative w.r.t. \(x\), and integrate w.r.t. \(y\) to solve for \(v_y\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Formulate mass flux in x-direction:
    \[\rho v_x = \left(\frac{1}{x}\right) x^2 = x \]
  2. Substitute into continuity equation:
    \[\frac{\partial(x)}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\frac{1}{x} \cdot v_y\right) = 0 \]\[1 + \frac{1}{x}\frac{\partial v_y}{\partial y} = 0 \]
    Note: \(\dfrac{1}{x}\) is treated as a constant when differentiating partially w.r.t. \(y\).
  3. Isolate the derivative of \(v_y\):
    \[\frac{1}{x}\frac{\partial v_y}{\partial y} = -1 \implies \frac{\partial v_y}{\partial y} = -x \]
  4. Integrate partially w.r.t. \(y\):
    \[v_y = -xy + f(x) \]
    where \(f(x)\) is an arbitrary function of \(x\). For the simplest flow field where \(f(x) = 0\): \(v_y = -xy\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(v_y = -xy\)  |  Correct option: (C)

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Steady incompressible flow
    • Closed conduit of uniform cross-section
  • Aim: Identify the hydraulic parameter that definitively decreases in the direction of flow.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Bernoulli's Equation with Head Loss: \[H_1 = H_2 + h_L \implies H_1 > H_2 \] where Total Head \(H = \dfrac{P}{\gamma} + Z + \dfrac{v^2}{2g}\)
  • Piezometric Head (\(h_p\)): \[h_p = \frac{P}{\gamma} + Z \]

4. Solution Method:

In a uniform conduit with incompressible flow, continuity requires constant velocity throughout. Analyze how this affects the total energy gradient.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Continuity for uniform cross-section:
    \[A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2 \implies v_1 = v_2 = v \]
    Velocity head \(\dfrac{v^2}{2g}\) is constant at all points.
  2. Energy equation between points 1 and 2:
    \[\left(\frac{P_1}{\gamma} + Z_1 + \frac{v^2}{2g}\right) - \left(\frac{P_2}{\gamma} + Z_2 + \frac{v^2}{2g}\right) = h_L \]
  3. Cancel constant velocity head:
    \[\left(\frac{P_1}{\gamma} + Z_1\right) - \left(\frac{P_2}{\gamma} + Z_2\right) = h_L > 0 \]\[(h_p)_1 - (h_p)_2 = h_L \]
    Since \(h_L > 0\) always, \((h_p)_1 > (h_p)_2\). Flow proceeds from higher to lower piezometric head.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: from higher to lower piezometric head  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q28
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A circular pipe has a diameter of 1 m, bed slope of 1 in 1000, and Manning’s roughness coefficient equal to 0.01. It may be treated as an open channel flow when it is flowing just full, i.e., the water level just touches the crest. The discharge in this condition is denoted by \(Q_{full}\). Similarly, the discharge when the pipe is flowing half-full, i.e., with a flow depth of 0.5 m, is denoted by \(Q_{half}\). The ratio \(Q_{full} / Q_{half}\) is:
questions.explanation:
Water Resources Engineering | Open Channel Flow

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Pipe diameter: \(D = 1\text{ m}\)
    • Bed slope: \(S = 1/1000\) (constant)
    • Manning's \(n = 0.01\) (constant)
    • Condition 1: Flowing just full (\(Q_{full}\)) — treated as open channel
    • Condition 2: Flowing half-full, depth = \(0.5\text{ m}\) (\(Q_{half}\))
  • Aim: Compute the ratio \(Q_{full} / Q_{half}\).

3. Core Concepts:

Manning's Equation: \[Q = \frac{1}{n} A R^{2/3} \sqrt{S} \] where \(R = A/P\) is the hydraulic radius. When a pipe flows just full as an open channel, atmospheric pressure acts at the crown and the entire perimeter is wetted (\(P = \pi D\)).

4. Solution Method:

Find \(A\), \(P\), and \(R\) for both configurations. Apply Manning's equation and compute the discharge ratio.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Just Full Flow (\(Q_{full}\)):
    \[A_{full} = \frac{\pi}{4}D^2, \quad P_{full} = \pi D \]\[R_{full} = \frac{A_{full}}{P_{full}} = \frac{\pi D^2/4}{\pi D} = \frac{D}{4} \]
  2. Half-Full Flow (\(Q_{half}\)):
    \[A_{half} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{4}D^2 = \frac{\pi}{8}D^2, \quad P_{half} = \frac{\pi D}{2} \]\[R_{half} = \frac{\pi D^2/8}{\pi D/2} = \frac{D}{4} \]
    Note: Both conditions share the identical hydraulic radius \(R = D/4\).
  3. Calculate the discharge ratio:
    Since \(R_{full} = R_{half}\), the \(R^{2/3}\) terms cancel:
    \[\frac{Q_{full}}{Q_{half}} = \frac{A_{full}}{A_{half}} = \frac{\pi D^2/4}{\pi D^2/8} = 2 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.question:
The smallest and largest Eigen values of the following matrix are:

\[\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 & 2 \\ 4 & -4 & 6 \\ 2 & -3 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \]
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra / Eigenvalues

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: A \(3 \times 3\) square matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 & 2 \\ 4 & -4 & 6 \\ 2 & -3 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\)
  • Aim: To determine the smallest and largest eigenvalues of the matrix.

3. Core Concepts:

Trace of a Matrix: The sum of the main diagonal elements equals the sum of the eigenvalues: \(\sum \lambda_i = \text{Trace}(A)\)

Determinant of a Matrix: Equals the product of the eigenvalues: \(\prod \lambda_i = \det(A)\)

Characteristic Equation: \[\lambda^3 - S_1\lambda^2 + S_2\lambda - S_3 = 0\] where:

  • \(S_1 = \text{Trace}(A)\)
  • \(S_2 = \text{Sum of principal minors of order 2}\)
  • \(S_3 = \det(A)\)

4. Solution Method:

Instead of fully solving the cubic equation, we calculate the Trace and Determinant and cross-check the options. This is a common time-saving trick in GATE.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate the Trace (\(S_1\)):
    \[S_1 = 3 + (-4) + 5 = 4 \]
    Thus, \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 + \lambda_3 = 4\)
  2. Calculate the Determinant (\(S_3\)):
    \[ \det(A) = 3[(-4)(5) - (6)(-3)] - (-2)[(4)(5) - (6)(2)] + 2[(4)(-3) - (-4)(2)] \]\[ = 3[-20 + 18] + 2[20 - 12] + 2[-12 + 8] \]\[= 3(-2) + 2(8) + 2(-4) = -6 + 16 - 8 = 2 \]
    Thus, \(\lambda_1 \times \lambda_2 \times \lambda_3 = 2\)
  3. Test the given options:
    OptionTwo EigenvaluesThird Eigenvalue (Sum = 4)Product Check (Must = 2)Result
    (A)1.5 and 2.5\(4 - 1.5 - 2.5 = 0\)\(1.5 \times 2.5 \times 0 = 0\)❌ Contradicts det = 2
    (B)0.5 and 2.5\(4 - 0.5 - 2.5 = 1.0\)\(0.5 \times 2.5 \times 1.0 = 1.25\)❌ Contradicts det = 2
    (C)1.0 and 3.0\(4 - 1.0 - 3.0 = 0\)\(1.0 \times 3.0 \times 0 = 0\)❌ Contradicts det = 2
    (D)1.0 and 2.0\(4 - 1.0 - 2.0 = 1.0\)\(1.0 \times 2.0 \times 1.0 = 2\)✅ Satisfies both conditions!

    The exact eigenvalues are 1, 1, and 2.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.0 and 2.0  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q37

questions.question: The quadratic equation \(x^2 - 4x + 4 = 0\) is to be solved numerically, starting with the initial guess \(x_0 = 3\). The Newton-Raphson method is applied once to get a new estimate and then the Secant method is applied once using the initial guess and this new estimate. The estimated value of the root after the application of the Secant method is __________.
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Function: \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 4 = 0\)
    • Initial guess: \(x_0 = 3\)
    • Algorithm: 1 iteration of Newton-Raphson (NR), followed by 1 iteration of the Secant method.
  • Aim: Find the estimated value of the root after the Secant iteration.

3. Core Concepts:

Newton-Raphson Method: \[x_{n+1} = x_n - \frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)} \]

Secant Method: \[ x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n) \left[\frac{x_n - x_{n-1}}{f(x_n) - f(x_{n-1})} \right] \]

4. Solution Method:

First, find \(x_1\) using the NR method with \(x_0\). Then, use \(x_0\) and \(x_1\) as the two initial conditions required to execute a single iteration of the Secant method to find \(x_2\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. First iteration using Newton-Raphson:
    Derivative: \(f'(x) = 2x - 4\)
    Evaluate at \(x_0 = 3\):
    \[f(3) = (3)^2 - 4(3) + 4 = 9 - 12 + 4 = 1 \]\[f'(3) = 2(3) - 4 = 6 - 4 = 2 \]\[x_1 = x_0 - \frac{f(x_0)}{f'(x_0)} = 3 - \frac{1}{2} = 2.5 \]
  2. Second iteration using Secant Method:
    Inputs: \(x_0 = 3\), \(x_1 = 2.5\)
    Evaluate \(f(x)\) at \(x_1\):
    \[f(2.5) = (2.5)^2 - 4(2.5) + 4 = 6.25 - 10 + 4 = 0.25 \]
    We already know \(f(x_0) = f(3) = 1\).

    Apply Secant formula:
    \[ x_2 = x_1 - f(x_1) \left[\frac{x_1 - x_0}{f(x_1) - f(x_0)} \right] \]\[ x_2 = 2.5 - 0.25 \left[\frac{2.5 - 3}{0.25 - 1} \right] = 2.5 - 0.25 \left[\frac{-0.5}{-0.75} \right] = 2.5 - 0.25 \left( \frac{2}{3} \right) \]\[x_2 = 2.5 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{15}{6} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{14}{6} = \frac{7}{3} \approx 2.333 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.333  |  Accepted key range: 2.32 to 2.34

questions.question:
Consider the following differential equation:

\[x(ydx + xdy) \cos\frac{y}{x} = y(xdy - ydx) \sin\frac{y}{x} \]

Which of the following is the solution of the above equation (c is an arbitrary constant)?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: \[x(y\,dx + x\,dy)\cos\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) = y(x\,dy - y\,dx)\sin\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) \]
  • Aim: Find the general solution of the differential equation.

3. Core Concepts:

  • This is a homogeneous first-order, first-degree differential equation.
  • Standard substitution technique: \(y = vx \implies dy = v\,dx + x\,dv\)

4. Solution Method:

Substitute \(y = vx\) and isolate variables \(x\) and \(v\) to perform direct integration.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Make the substitution:
    Let \(y = vx\), so \(dy = v\,dx + x\,dv\).

    LHS:
    \[ x[(vx)\,dx + x(v\,dx + x\,dv)]\cos(v) = x[2vx\,dx + x^2\,dv]\cos(v) = x^2(2v\cos v\,dx + x\cos v\,dv) \]
    RHS:
    \[ (vx)[x(v\,dx + x\,dv) - (vx)\,dx]\sin(v) = vx[vx\,dx + x^2\,dv - vx\,dx]\sin(v) = x^3 v\sin v\,dv \]
  2. Equate LHS and RHS and separate variables:
    \[x^2(2v\cos v\,dx + x\cos v\,dv) = x^3 v\sin v\,dv \]
    Divide through by \(x^2\):
    \[2v\cos v\,dx + x\cos v\,dv = xv\sin v\,dv \]\[2v\cos v\,dx = x(v\sin v - \cos v)\,dv \]
    Isolate \(x\) on one side and \(v\) on the other:
    \[2\frac{dx}{x} = \left(\frac{v\sin v - \cos v}{v\cos v}\right)dv = \left(\frac{\sin v}{\cos v} - \frac{1}{v}\right)dv = \left(\tan v - \frac{1}{v}\right)dv \]
  3. Integrate both sides:
    \[\int \frac{2}{x}\,dx = \int \tan v\,dv - \int \frac{1}{v}\,dv \]\[2\ln(x) = -\ln(\cos v) - \ln(v) + \ln(C) \]
    Note: \(\int \tan v\,dv = \ln(\sec v) = -\ln(\cos v)\)
    \[\ln(x^2) + \ln(v) + \ln(\cos v) = \ln(C) \]\[\ln(x^2 \cdot v \cdot \cos v) = \ln(C) \]
  4. Re-substitute \(v = y/x\):
    \[x^2 \left(\frac{y}{x}\right)\cos\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) = C \implies xy\cos\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) = C \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(xy\cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = c\)  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Consider the following complex function:

\[f(z) = \frac{9}{(z - 1)(z + 2)^2} \]

Which of the following is one of the residues of the above function?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Complex Variables

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Complex function \[f(z) = \frac{9}{(z-1)(z+2)^2} \]
  • Aim: Evaluate one of the residues of the function.

3. Core Concepts:

Poles: The function has singularities where the denominator is zero.

  • Simple pole (order \(m=1\)) at \(z = 1\)
  • Pole of order \(m=2\) at \(z = -2\)

Residue at Simple Pole (\(z=a\)): \[\text{Res}(z=a) = \lim_{z \to a}(z-a)f(z) \]

Residue at Pole of Order \(m\) (\(z=a\)): \[ \text{Res}(z=a) = \frac{1}{(m-1)!}\lim_{z \to a}\frac{d^{m-1}}{dz^{m-1}}\left[(z-a)^m f(z)\right] \]

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the residues at both \(z=1\) and \(z=-2\), then check which calculated value matches one of the multiple-choice options.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Residue at the simple pole \(z = 1\):
    \[ R_1 = \lim_{z \to 1}(z-1)\left[\frac{9}{(z-1)(z+2)^2}\right] = \lim_{z \to 1}\frac{9}{(z+2)^2} = \frac{9}{(1+2)^2} = \frac{9}{9} = 1 \]
  2. Residue at the pole of order 2 (\(z = -2\)):
    \[ R_{-2} = \frac{1}{(2-1)!}\lim_{z \to -2}\frac{d}{dz}\left[(z+2)^2 \cdot \frac{9}{(z-1)(z+2)^2}\right] \]\[ = \lim_{z \to -2}\frac{d}{dz}\left[9(z-1)^{-1}\right] = \lim_{z \to -2}\left[-9(z-1)^{-2}\right] = \frac{-9}{(-2-1)^2} = \frac{-9}{9} = -1 \]
  3. Map to Options:
    The calculated residues are \(1\) and \(-1\). Option (A) presents \(-1\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(-1\)  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q40

questions.question: The directional derivative of the field \(u(x, y, z) = x^2 - 3yz\) in the direction of the vector \((\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k})\) at point (2, -1, 4) is __________.
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Vector Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Scalar field: \(u(x,y,z) = x^2 - 3yz\)
    • Direction Vector: \(\vec{v} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\)
    • Point of evaluation: \(P(2, -1, 4)\)
  • Aim: Calculate the directional derivative of the field \(u\) in the direction of vector \(\vec{v}\).

3. Core Concepts:

Gradient Vector (\( abla u\)): The vector representing the maximum rate of change.
\[ abla u = rac{\partial u}{\partial x}\hat{i} + rac{\partial u}{\partial y}\hat{j} + rac{\partial u}{\partial z}\hat{k} \]

Directional Derivative (\(D_{\vec{v}}u\)): The dot product of the gradient at the specified point and the unit vector in the direction of interest.
\[D_{\vec{v}}u = abla u \cdot \hat{n}, \quad ext{where } \hat{n} = rac{\vec{v}}{|\vec{v}|} \]

4. Solution Method:

Find the gradient vector and evaluate it at coordinates \((2,-1,4)\). Calculate the unit direction vector. Finally, take the scalar dot product of the two.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compute Gradient (\( abla u\)):
    \[ rac{\partial u}{\partial x} = 2x, \quad rac{\partial u}{\partial y} = -3z, \quad rac{\partial u}{\partial z} = -3y \]\[ abla u = 2x\hat{i} - 3z\hat{j} - 3y\hat{k} \]
    Evaluate at point \(P(2,-1,4)\):
    \[ abla u = 2(2)\hat{i} - 3(4)\hat{j} - 3(-1)\hat{k} = 4\hat{i} - 12\hat{j} + 3\hat{k} \]
  2. Obtain the Unit Direction Vector (\(\hat{n}\)):
    \[\vec{v} = 1\hat{i} + 1\hat{j} - 2\hat{k} \]\[|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{1+1+4} = \sqrt{6} \]\[\hat{n} = rac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}) \]
  3. Calculate the Dot Product:
    \[ D_{\vec{v}}u = (4\hat{i} - 12\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) \cdot \left[ rac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}) ight] \]\[ = rac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[(4 imes 1) + (-12 imes 1) + (3 imes -2)] = rac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[4 - 12 - 6] = rac{-14}{\sqrt{6}} \approx -5.715 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(-5.715\)  |  Accepted key range: \(-5.72\) to \(-5.70\)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question:
The composition of an air-entrained concrete is given below:

Water : 184 kg/m³
Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC): 368 kg/m³
Sand : 606 kg/m³
Coarse aggregate : 1155 kg/m³

Assume the specific gravity of OPC, sand and coarse aggregate to be 3.14, 2.67 and 2.74, respectively. The air content is __________ liters/ m³.
questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Concrete Mix Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Mix amounts per m³ of concrete:
    IngredientMass (kg)Specific Gravity (SG)
    Water1841.00
    OPC (Cement)3683.14
    Sand6062.67
    Coarse Aggregate (CA)11552.74
  • Aim: Find the entrapped air content per cubic meter in liters.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Absolute Volume Method (IS 10262 basis): The sum of the absolute solid volumes of all ingredients plus the volume of air must equal the total gross volume of freshly mixed concrete (\(1\text{ m}^3\)).
  • Volume Calculation: \[\text{Absolute Volume } (V) = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Specific Gravity} \times \text{Density of Water}} \]
  • Density of water \(\gamma_w = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3\)
  • \(1\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ liters}\)

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the absolute volume of each individual ingredient in m³. Sum these volumes. The difference between the theoretical target yield (\(1\text{ m}^3\)) and the absolute solid volume sum is the volume occupied by air. Convert that difference into liters.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate absolute volumes (in m³):
    \[V_{\text{water}} = \frac{184}{1 \times 1000} = 0.184000\text{ m}^3 \]\[V_{\text{cement}} = \frac{368}{3.14 \times 1000} = 0.117197\text{ m}^3 \]\[V_{\text{sand}} = \frac{606}{2.67 \times 1000} = 0.226966\text{ m}^3 \]\[V_{\text{CA}} = \frac{1155}{2.74 \times 1000} = 0.421533\text{ m}^3 \]
  2. Sum the solid volumes:
    \[V_{\text{solid}} = 0.184000 + 0.117197 + 0.226966 + 0.421533 = 0.949696\text{ m}^3 \]
  3. Find air volume and convert to liters:
    Target volume of concrete batch is \(1\text{ m}^3\).
    \[V_{\text{air}} = 1.0 - 0.949696 = 0.050304\text{ m}^3 \]\[\text{Air content in liters} = 0.050304 \times 1000 = 50.304\text{ liters} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 50.3 liters  |  Accepted key range: 49.5 to 51.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q42
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: A bracket plate connected to a column flange transmits a load of 100 kN as shown in the following figure. The maximum force for which the bolts should be designed is __________ kN.
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Bolted Connections

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Eccentric Load: \(P = 100\text{ kN}\)
    • Eccentricity from bolt group CG: \(e = 600\text{ mm}\)
    • Number of bolts: \(n = 5\)
    • Bolt arrangement: Quincunx pattern (like '5' on a dice) with horizontal spacing \(75\text{ mm}\) and vertical spacing \(75\text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the maximum resultant force on the most critically stressed bolt.

3. Core Concepts:

For an eccentrically loaded bolted connection (in-plane), the force on any bolt is the vector sum of:

  1. Direct Shear Force (\(\vec{F_d}\)): Assumed to be shared equally among all bolts. \[F_d = \frac{P}{n} \]
  2. Torsional Shear Force (\(\vec{F_t}\)): Arises due to the moment \(M = P \times e\). The force on a specific bolt is proportional to its radial distance \(r_i\) from the CG of the bolt group. \[\vec{F_t} = \frac{\vec{M} \times \vec{r_i}}{\sum r_i^2} \] In scalar components: \(F_{tx} = \dfrac{M \cdot y_i}{\sum r_i^2}\) and \(F_{ty} = \dfrac{M \cdot x_i}{\sum r_i^2}\)
  3. Resultant Force (\(F_R\)): \[F_R = \sqrt{(\sum F_x)^2 + (\sum F_y)^2} \]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Coordinate Geometry of Bolt Group:
    Assign the origin \((0,0)\) to the central bolt (CG of the group). The coordinates \((x_i, y_i)\) of the 5 bolts are:
    Bolt\(x_i\) (mm)\(y_i\) (mm)
    Top-Right7575
    Bottom-Right75-75
    Top-Left-7575
    Bottom-Left-75-75
    Center00

    \[\sum r_i^2 = 4 \times (75^2 + 75^2) + 0 = 4 \times (5625 + 5625) = 45000\text{ mm}^2 \]
  2. Direct Shear Force (\(F_d\)):
    \[F_d = \frac{100\text{ kN}}{5} = 20\text{ kN (acting downwards, i.e., } -y\text{ direction)} \]
  3. Torsional Shear Force on Critical Bolt (Top-Right at \((75, 75)\)):
    Applied moment (clockwise): \(M = P \times e = 100 \times 600 = 60000\text{ kN-mm}\)
    \[F_{tx} = \frac{M \cdot y}{\sum r_i^2} = \frac{60000 \times 75}{45000} = 100\text{ kN (rightwards)} \]\[F_{ty} = \frac{M \cdot x}{\sum r_i^2} = \frac{60000 \times 75}{45000} = 100\text{ kN (downwards)} \]
    Note: The Bottom-Right bolt at \((75,-75)\) experiences \(F_{tx} = 100\text{ kN}\) leftwards and \(F_{ty} = 100\text{ kN}\) downwards — the vertical summation is identical, making both right-side bolts equally critical.
  4. Resultant Force (\(F_R\)) for Top-Right Bolt:
    • Total X-force: \(F_x = F_{tx} = 100\text{ kN}\)
    • Total Y-force: \(F_y = F_{ty} + F_d = 100 + 20 = 120\text{ kN}\)
    \[F_R = \sqrt{F_x^2 + F_y^2} = \sqrt{100^2 + 120^2} = \sqrt{10000 + 14400} = \sqrt{24400} \approx 156.205\text{ kN} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 156.20 kN  |  Accepted key range: 155 to 156.3

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q43
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: Consider the singly reinforced beam section given below (left figure). The stress block parameters for the cross-section from IS:456-2000 are also given below (right figure). The moment of resistance for the given section by the limit state method is __________ kN-m.
questions.explanation:
RCC Structures | Flexure Limit State

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Beam dimensions: Width \(b = 200\text{ mm}\), Effective depth \(d = 300\text{ mm}\)
    • Materials: Concrete M25 (\(f_{ck} = 25\text{ MPa}\)), Steel Fe415 (\(f_y = 415\text{ MPa}\))
    • Tension Reinforcement: 4 bars of \(12\text{ mm}\) diameter (\(4\text{-}12\Phi\))
  • Aim: Calculate the Moment of Resistance (\(M_u\)) of the section using the Limit State Method.

3. Core Concepts:

According to IS 456:2000 (Annex G):

  1. Area of Steel (\(A_{st}\)): \[A_{st} = n \times \frac{\pi}{4} \times \phi^2 \]
  2. Depth of Neutral Axis (\(x_u\)): Found by equating total compression to total tension: \[0.36\, f_{ck}\, b\, x_u = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st} \]
  3. Limiting Neutral Axis Depth (\(x_{u,max}\)): For Fe415 steel, \(x_{u,max} = 0.48d\)
  4. Moment of Resistance (\(M_u\)): If \(x_u < x_{u,max}\) (Under-reinforced): \[M_u = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st}\,(d - 0.42\, x_u) \]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Area of Steel (\(A_{st}\)):
    \[A_{st} = 4 \times \frac{\pi}{4} \times (12)^2 = 452.39\text{ mm}^2 \]
  2. Find Actual Neutral Axis Depth (\(x_u\)):
    \[x_u = \frac{0.87\, f_y\, A_{st}}{0.36\, f_{ck}\, b} = \frac{0.87 \times 415 \times 452.39}{0.36 \times 25 \times 200} = \frac{163335.8}{1800} = 90.74\text{ mm} \]
  3. Section Classification:
    \[x_{u,max} = 0.48 \times 300 = 144\text{ mm} \]
    Since \(x_u = 90.74\text{ mm} < x_{u,max} = 144\text{ mm}\), the section is under-reinforced.
    Sanity Check: For an under-reinforced section, steel yields before concrete crushes — using \(0.87f_y\) is strictly valid.
  4. Calculate Moment of Resistance (\(M_u\)):
    \[M_u = 0.87\, f_y\, A_{st}\,(d - 0.42\, x_u) \]\[M_u = 163335.8 \times (300 - 0.42 \times 90.74) \]\[M_u = 163335.8 \times (300 - 38.11) = 163335.8 \times 261.89 \]\[M_u = 42{,}776{,}013\text{ N-mm} = 42.78\text{ kN-m} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 42.78 kN-m  |  Accepted key range: 42 to 43

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: For formation of collapse mechanism in the following figure, the minimum value of \(P_u\) is \(cM_p/L\). \(M_p\) and \(3M_p\) denote the plastic moment capacities of beam sections as shown in this figure. The value of c is __________.
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Plastic Analysis

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Fixed-fixed continuous beam subjected to a point load \(P_u\)
    • Left segment: Length \(= 2\text{ m}\), Plastic moment capacity \(= 3M_p\)
    • Right segment: Total length \(= 1\text{ m} + 1\text{ m} = 2\text{ m}\), Plastic moment capacity \(= M_p\)
    • Load \(P_u\) applied in the middle of the right segment (at \(3\text{ m}\) from the left support)
  • Aim: Find the coefficient \(c\) for the minimum collapse load given by \(P_u = c\,\dfrac{M_p}{L}\).
    Note: The problem dimensionally implies \(L\) is a unit length placeholder of 1 meter to map to the diagram's explicit meter units.

3. Core Concepts:

To find the true collapse load, we apply the Kinematic Method (Mechanism Method) of plastic analysis. We equate External Work (EW) to Internal Work (IW) for all possible independent and combined mechanisms. The one yielding the minimum \(P_u\) is the true collapse mechanism.

  • \(EW = \sum P_i \delta_i\)
  • \(IW = \sum M_{pi}\,\theta_i\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Mechanism 1: Global Collapse
    Plastic hinges form at: Left Support A (capacity \(3M_p\)), under the load C (capacity \(M_p\)), and at Right Support D (capacity \(M_p\)). Let deflection under load = \(\Delta\).
    • Segment AC length \(= 3\text{ m}\): \(\theta_A = \dfrac{\Delta}{3}\)
    • Segment CD length \(= 1\text{ m}\): \(\theta_D = \Delta = 3\theta_A\)
    • Relative rotation at hinge C: \(\theta_C = \theta_A + \theta_D = 4\theta_A\)
    \[EW = P_u \times \Delta = P_u(3\theta_A) \]\[IW = 3M_p(\theta_A) + M_p(4\theta_A) + M_p(3\theta_A) = 10M_p\theta_A \]\[EW = IW \implies P_u = \frac{10}{3}M_p = 3.333\,M_p \]
    Verification: The moment at the step-change B (2 m from left): \(M_B = -3M_p + \frac{2}{3}(4M_p) = -0.333M_p\). Since \(|-0.333M_p| < M_p\), the section is safe — this mechanism is statically admissible.
  2. Mechanism 2: Local Collapse of the Right Segment
    Plastic hinges form at: Step-change B (capacity \(M_p\)), under the load C (capacity \(M_p\)), and at Right Support D (capacity \(M_p\)). The left segment AB remains rigid.
    • Segment BC length \(= 1\text{ m}\): \(\theta_B = \Delta\)
    • Segment CD length \(= 1\text{ m}\): \(\theta_D = \Delta\)
    • Relative rotation at C: \(\theta_C = \theta_B + \theta_D = 2\Delta\)
    \[EW = P_u \times \Delta \]\[IW = M_p(\Delta) + M_p(2\Delta) + M_p(\Delta) = 4M_p\Delta \]\[EW = IW \implies P_u = 4M_p \]
  3. Conclusion:
    Comparing both mechanisms:
    MechanismCollapse Load \(P_u\)
    Global Collapse\(3.333\,M_p\) ← Minimum (Governs)
    Local Collapse (Right)\(4.0\,M_p\)

    Matching \(P_u = c\,\dfrac{M_p}{L}\) with \(L = 1\text{ m}\): \(c = 3.33\)

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3.33  |  Accepted key range: 3.30 to 3.40

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q45
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A tapered circular rod of diameter varying from 20 mm to 10 mm is connected to another uniform circular rod of diameter 10 mm as shown in the following figure. Both bars are made of same material with the modulus of elasticity, \(E = 2\times10^5\) MPa. When subjected to a load \(P = 30\pi\) kN, the deflection at point A is __________ mm.
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Axial Deformation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Tapered rod: Length \(L_1 = 2\text{ m} = 2000\text{ mm}\), Diameters \(d_1 = 20\text{ mm}\), \(d_2 = 10\text{ mm}\)
    • Uniform rod: Length \(L_2 = 1.5\text{ m} = 1500\text{ mm}\), Diameter \(d_2 = 10\text{ mm}\)
    • Material properties: Modulus of elasticity \(E = 2 \times 10^5\text{ MPa}\)
    • Applied load: \(P = 30\pi\text{ kN} = 30\pi \times 10^3\text{ N}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the total axial deflection at the free end (point A) in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Principle of Superposition: The total deflection of a stepped bar is the sum of the individual deflections of its sections: \(\Delta = \Delta_1 + \Delta_2\)
  • Elongation of a Uniform Circular Bar: \[\Delta_{\text{uniform}} = \frac{PL}{AE} = \frac{4PL}{\pi E d^2} \]
  • Elongation of a Tapered Circular Bar: \[\Delta_{\text{tapered}} = \frac{4PL}{\pi E\, d_1\, d_2} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the deflection of the tapered rod section (\(\Delta_1\)).
  2. Calculate the deflection of the uniform rod section (\(\Delta_2\)).
  3. Add both deflections to find the total displacement at point A.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Deflection of the tapered rod (\(\Delta_1\)):
    \[\Delta_1 = \frac{4PL_1}{\pi E\,d_1\,d_2} = \frac{4 \times (30\pi \times 10^3) \times 2000}{\pi \times (2 \times 10^5) \times 20 \times 10} = \frac{240 \times 10^6 \pi}{40 \times 10^6 \pi} = 6\text{ mm} \]
  2. Deflection of the uniform rod (\(\Delta_2\)):
    \[\Delta_2 = \frac{4PL_2}{\pi E\,d_2^2} = \frac{4 \times (30\pi \times 10^3) \times 1500}{\pi \times (2 \times 10^5) \times (10)^2} = \frac{180 \times 10^6 \pi}{20 \times 10^6 \pi} = 9\text{ mm} \]
  3. Total Deflection at point A:
    \[\Delta_{\text{total}} = \Delta_1 + \Delta_2 = 6\text{ mm} + 9\text{ mm} = 15\text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 15 mm  |  Accepted key range: 14.5 to 15.5

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: Two beams are connected by a linear spring as shown in the following figure. For a load P as shown in the figure, the percentage of the applied load P carried by the spring is __________.
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Indeterminate Structures

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Two identical cantilever beams with flexural rigidity \(EI\) and length \(L\)
    • A linear spring connects the free ends of the two beams
    • Spring stiffness: \(K_s = \dfrac{3EI}{2L^3}\)
    • External downward load \(P\) applied at the free end of the top beam
  • Aim: Find the percentage of the applied load \(P\) that is carried by the spring.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Compatibility Condition: The relative displacement between the free ends of the two beams must equal the deformation of the spring.
  • Deflection of a Cantilever Beam: A point load \(W\) at the free end causes a deflection: \[\Delta = \frac{WL^3}{3EI} \]
  • Hooke's Law for Springs: \(F_s = K_s \cdot \Delta_s\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Let the internal force in the spring be \(F_s\). The spring pulls down on the top beam and pulls up on the bottom beam.
  2. Formulate the downward deflection of each beam.
  3. Express the spring compression as \(\Delta_s = \Delta_1 - \Delta_2\).
  4. Substitute into the compatibility equation and solve for \(F_s\) as a fraction of \(P\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Beam Deflections:
    • Top Beam (net downward load \(= P - F_s\)): \[\Delta_1 = \frac{(P - F_s)L^3}{3EI} \]
    • Bottom Beam (net downward load \(= F_s\)): \[\Delta_2 = \frac{F_s L^3}{3EI} \]
  2. Spring Deformation:
    \[\Delta_s = \Delta_1 - \Delta_2 = \frac{F_s}{K_s} \]
  3. Compatibility Equation:
    \[\frac{(P - F_s)L^3}{3EI} - \frac{F_s L^3}{3EI} = \frac{F_s}{K_s} \]
    Substituting \(K_s = \dfrac{3EI}{2L^3}\) (i.e., \(\dfrac{1}{K_s} = \dfrac{2L^3}{3EI}\)):
    \[\frac{P \cdot L^3}{3EI} - \frac{2F_s \cdot L^3}{3EI} = F_s \cdot \frac{2L^3}{3EI} \]
    Dividing throughout by \(\dfrac{L^3}{3EI}\):
    \[P - 2F_s = 2F_s \implies P = 4F_s \implies F_s = 0.25P \]
  4. Percentage Calculation:
    \[\text{Percentage} = \frac{F_s}{P} \times 100 = 0.25 \times 100 = 25\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 25%

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: For the 2D truss with the applied loads shown below, the strain energy in the member XY is __________ kN-m. For member XY, assume AE = 30 kN, where A is cross-section area and E is the modulus of elasticity.
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Truss & Strain Energy

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • 2D Truss geometry: Panel width \(= 3\text{ m}\), panel height \(= 3\text{ m}\)
    • Loads at top node: \(10\text{ kN}\) (Horizontal \(\rightarrow\)), \(5\text{ kN}\) (Vertical \(\downarrow\))
    • Target member: \(XY\) (Horizontal member at height \(6\text{ m}\))
    • Axial rigidity: \(AE = 30\text{ kN}\), Length of member \(XY\): \(L = 3\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the axial strain energy in member \(XY\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Method of Joints: Resolving forces at nodes using \(\sum F_x = 0\) and \(\sum F_y = 0\) to find axial forces in members.
  • Strain Energy due to Axial Force: \[U = \frac{P_{\text{axial}}^2\, L}{2AE} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Trace the geometry: Diagonals run from top-left to bottom-right across the vertical panels.
  2. Isolate the topmost node to find the internal force in the top diagonal member.
  3. Move to node \(Y\) and apply equilibrium equations to find the axial force in horizontal member \(XY\).
  4. Calculate the strain energy using the derived force.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Coordinate Geometry:
    Let the hinge support be the origin \((0,0)\).
    • Top loaded node \(D\): \((0,9)\)
    • Node \(Y\): \((3,6)\)
    • Node \(X\): \((0,6)\)
    The top panel features a diagonal member connecting \(D(0,9)\) to \(Y(3,6)\).
  2. Equilibrium at Top Node \(D(0,9)\):
    Applied loads: \(10\text{ kN}\) (\(+x\)), \(5\text{ kN}\) (\(-y\)).
    Members at \(D\): vertical member \(DX\) and diagonal member \(DY\).
    Unit vector from \(D\) to \(Y\):
    \[\hat{u}_{DY} = \frac{(3)\hat{i} + (-3)\hat{j}}{\sqrt{3^2+3^2}} = \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \]
    Let \(F_{DY}\) be the force in member \(DY\) (tension positive):
    \[\sum F_x = 0 \implies 10 + F_{DY}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 0 \implies F_{DY} = -10\sqrt{2}\text{ kN (Compression)} \]
  3. Equilibrium at Node \(Y(3,6)\):
    The compressed diagonal \(DY\) pushes node \(Y\) in the \((+x, -y)\) direction.
    Horizontal push from \(DY\) on \(Y\): \(|-10\sqrt{2}| \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 10\text{ kN}\) (\(\rightarrow\))
    Let \(F_{XY}\) be the force in horizontal member \(XY\) (tension pulls \(Y\) in \(-x\) direction):
    \[\sum F_x = 0 \implies 10 - F_{XY} = 0 \implies F_{XY} = 10\text{ kN} \]
  4. Strain Energy Calculation:
    \[U_{XY} = \frac{F_{XY}^2 \cdot L}{2AE} = \frac{(10)^2 \times 3}{2 \times 30} = \frac{300}{60} = 5\text{ kN-m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 5 kN-m

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q48
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.question: An earth embankment is to be constructed with compacted cohesionless soil. The volume of the embankment is 5000 m³ and the target dry unit weight is 16.2 kN/m³. Three nearby sites (see figure below) have been identified from where the required soil can be transported to the construction site. The void ratios (e) of different sites are shown in the figure. Assume the specific gravity of soil to be 2.7 for all three sites. If the cost of transportation per km is twice the cost of excavation per m³ of borrow pits, which site would you choose as the most economic solution? (Use unit weight of water = 10 kN/m³)
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earthwork Cost Optimization

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Embankment: Volume \(V_{emb} = 5000\text{ m}^3\), Target dry unit weight \(\gamma_d = 16.2\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Borrow Pits Data:
      SiteVoid Ratio \((e)\)Distance \((D)\) km
      X0.60140
      Y0.7080
      Z0.64100
    • Soil Properties: \(G_s = 2.7\), \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Cost Relation: Cost of transportation per km (\(C_t\)) is twice the cost of excavation per m³ (\(C_e\)): \(C_t = 2C_e\)
  • Aim: Identify the most economical borrow pit site.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Phase Relationships: The volume of solid particles (\(V_s\)) remains constant during earthwork operations. \[\gamma_d = \frac{G_s\,\gamma_w}{1+e} \quad \text{and} \quad V_{\text{total}} = V_s(1+e) \]
  • Total Cost Formulation: \[\text{Total Cost} = (C_e \times V_{\text{site}}) + (C_t \times D_{\text{site}}) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the void ratio of the target embankment (\(e_{emb}\)).
  2. Calculate the invariant volume of solids (\(V_s\)) required.
  3. Compute the excavation volume required from each site.
  4. Evaluate the cost index function for all three pits to find the minimum.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Void ratio and Volume of solids for the embankment:
    \[16.2 = \frac{2.7 \times 10}{1+e_{emb}} \implies 1+e_{emb} = \frac{27}{16.2} = 1.6667 \implies e_{emb} = 0.6667 \]\[V_s = \frac{V_{emb}}{1+e_{emb}} = \frac{5000}{1.6667} = 3000\text{ m}^3 \]
  2. Excavation volumes required from each site:
    \[V_X = 3000(1 + 0.6) = 4800\text{ m}^3 \]\[V_Y = 3000(1 + 0.7) = 5100\text{ m}^3 \]\[V_Z = 3000(1 + 0.64) = 4920\text{ m}^3 \]
  3. Cost Function Optimization:
    Given \(C_t = 2C_e\), the total cost is:
    \[\text{Total Cost} = C_e \cdot V_{\text{site}} + 2C_e \cdot D_{\text{site}} = C_e(V_{\text{site}} + 2D_{\text{site}}) \]
    Minimize the cost index \(f = V_{\text{site}} + 2D_{\text{site}}\):
    Site\(V_{\text{site}}\) (m³)\(2D_{\text{site}}\) (km)Cost Index \(f\)
    X4800\(2 \times 140 = 280\)5080 ← Minimum
    Y5100\(2 \times 80 = 160\)5260
    Z4920\(2 \times 100 = 200\)5120
