questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A water tank is to be constructed on the soil deposit shown in the figure below. A circular footing of diameter 3 m and depth of embedment 1 m has been designed to support the tank. The total vertical load to be taken by the footing is 1500 kN. Assume the unit weight of water as 10 kN/m³ and the load dispersion pattern as 2V:1H. The expected settlement of the tank due to primary consolidation of the clay layer is __________ mm.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Consolidation)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Diameter of circular footing: \(D = 3\text{ m}\)
    • Depth of embedment: \(D_f = 1\text{ m}\)
    • Vertical load on footing: \(Q = 1500\text{ kN}\)
    • Load dispersion pattern: \(2V:1H\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Soil Profile:
      Depth (m)Soil TypeProperties
      0 to 2Silty Sand\(\gamma_{bulk} = 15\text{ kN/m}^3\) (GWT at 2 m)
      2 to 8Sand\(\gamma_{sat} = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\)
      8 to 18NC Clay\(\gamma_{sat} = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(C_c = 0.3\), \(e_0 = 0.7\)
  • Aim: Calculate the primary consolidation settlement of the clay layer in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Initial Effective Stress (\(\sigma_0'\)): Calculated at mid-depth of the clay layer. \[\sigma_0' = \sum(\gamma \cdot z) - u\]
  • Stress Increment (\(\Delta\sigma'\)): Using \(2V:1H\) dispersion: \[\Delta\sigma' = \frac{Q}{A_z} = \frac{Q}{\dfrac{\pi}{4}(D+z)^2}\] where \(z\) = depth from footing base to center of clay layer.
  • Primary Settlement (\(S_c\)): \[S_c = \frac{C_c H_0}{1+e_0}\log_{10}\left(\frac{\sigma_0' + \Delta\sigma'}{\sigma_0'}\right)\]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Locate the center of the clay layer:
    Thickness: \(H_0 = 18 - 8 = 10\text{ m}\)
    Depth to center from GL \(= 8 + \dfrac{10}{2} = 13\text{ m}\)
  2. Calculate Initial Effective Stress (\(\sigma_0'\)) at 13 m depth:
    \[\Delta\sigma_1' = 15 \times 2 = 30\text{ kPa} \quad (0\text{ to }2\text{ m, Silty Sand}) \]\[\Delta\sigma_2' = (18-10) \times 6 = 48\text{ kPa} \quad (2\text{ to }8\text{ m, Sand}) \]\[\Delta\sigma_3' = (18-10) \times 5 = 40\text{ kPa} \quad (8\text{ to }13\text{ m, Clay half-depth}) \]\[\sigma_0' = 30 + 48 + 40 = 118\text{ kPa} \]
  3. Calculate Stress Increment (\(\Delta\sigma'\)) at 13 m depth:
    Distance from footing base to center of clay: \(z = 13 - 1 = 12\text{ m}\)
    \[D_z = D + z = 3 + 12 = 15\text{ m} \]\[A_z = \frac{\pi}{4}(15)^2 = 176.715\text{ m}^2 \]\[\Delta\sigma' = \frac{1500}{176.715} = 8.488\text{ kPa} \]
  4. Calculate Consolidation Settlement (\(S_c\)):
    \(H_0 = 10\text{ m} = 10000\text{ mm}\)
    \[S_c = \frac{0.3 \times 10000}{1+0.7}\log_{10}\left(\frac{118 + 8.488}{118}\right) \]\[S_c = \frac{3000}{1.7}\log_{10}(1.0719) = 1764.706 \times 0.03016 = 53.23\text{ mm} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 53.23 mm  |  Accepted key range: 50.0 to 55.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A 20 m thick clay layer is sandwiched between a silty sand layer and a gravelly sand layer. The layer experiences 30 mm settlement in 2 years.

Given:
\[T_v = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\pi}{4} \left( \dfrac{U}{100} \right)^2 & \text{for } U \le 60\% \\ 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(100 - U) & \text{for } U > 60\% \end{cases} \]

where \(T_v\) is the time factor and \(U\) is the degree of consolidation in %.

If the coefficient of consolidation of the layer is 0.003 cm²/s, the deposit will experience a total of 50 mm settlement in the next __________ years.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Consolidation Time)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Thickness of clay: \(H = 20\text{ m}\) (sandwiched between sand layers → double drainage)
    • Settlement at \(t_1 = 2\text{ years}\): \(S_1 = 30\text{ mm}\)
    • Coefficient of consolidation: \(c_v = 0.003\text{ cm}^2/\text{s} = 3 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}\)
  • Aim: Find the additional time required to reach a total settlement \(S_2 = 50\text{ mm}\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Drainage path length: \(d = H/2 = 10\text{ m}\)
  • Time Factor: \(T_v = \dfrac{c_v t}{d^2}\)
  • For \(U \leq 60\%\): \(T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\left(\dfrac{U}{100}\right)^2\)
  • For \(U > 60\%\): \(T_v = 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(100-U)\)

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate \(T_{v1}\) at \(t_1 = 2\) years:
    \(t_1 = 2 \times 365 \times 24 \times 3600 = 6.3072 \times 10^7\text{ s}\)
    \[T_{v1} = \frac{(3 \times 10^{-7}) \times (6.3072 \times 10^7)}{(10)^2} = \frac{18.9216}{100} = 0.1892 \]
  2. Find Degree of Consolidation \(U_1\) and Ultimate Settlement \(S_f\):
    Since \(T_{v1} = 0.1892 < 0.282\), use: \(T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\left(\dfrac{U}{100}\right)^2\)
    \[\frac{U_1}{100} = \sqrt{\frac{0.1892 \times 4}{\pi}} = 0.4908 \implies U_1 = 49.08\% \]\[S_f = \frac{S_1}{U_1} = \frac{30}{0.4908} = 61.12\text{ mm} \]
  3. Find Time \(t_2\) for total settlement \(S_2 = 50\) mm:
    \[U_2 = \frac{50}{61.12} = 0.818 = 81.8\% \]
    Since \(U_2 > 60\%\), use the logarithmic equation:
    \[T_{v2} = 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(100 - 81.8) = 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(18.2) \]\[T_{v2} = 1.781 - 0.933(1.260) = 1.781 - 1.1756 = 0.6054 \]\[t_2 = \frac{T_{v2}\,d^2}{c_v} = \frac{0.6054 \times 100}{3 \times 10^{-7}} = 20.18 \times 10^7\text{ s} = 6.40\text{ years} \]
  4. Calculate additional time:
    \[\Delta t = t_2 - t_1 = 6.40 - 2.0 = 4.40\text{ years} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.40 years  |  Accepted key range: 4.0 to 5.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q51
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A non-homogeneous soil deposit consists of a silt layer sandwiched between a fine-sand layer at top and a clay layer below. Permeability of the silt layer is 10 times the permeability of the clay layer and one-tenth of the permeability of the sand layer. Thickness of the silt layer is 2 times the thickness of the sand layer and two-third of the thickness of the clay layer. The ratio of equivalent horizontal and equivalent vertical permeability of the deposit is __________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Permeability)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • 3 layers: Fine Sand (Top), Silt (Middle), Clay (Bottom)
    • Permeability relations: \(k_{silt} = 10\,k_{clay}\) and \(k_{silt} = 0.1\,k_{sand}\)
    • Thickness relations: \(H_{silt} = 2\,H_{sand}\) and \(H_{silt} = \dfrac{2}{3}\,H_{clay}\)
  • Aim: Find the ratio \(k_h / k_v\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Equivalent Horizontal Permeability (parallel to bedding): \[k_h = \frac{\sum(k_i H_i)}{\sum H_i} \]
  • Equivalent Vertical Permeability (perpendicular to bedding): \[k_v = \frac{\sum H_i}{\sum(H_i / k_i)} \]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Establish Relative Variables:
    Let \(k_{clay} = k\), then: \(k_{silt} = 10k\), \(k_{sand} = 10 \times k_{silt} = 100k\)
    Let \(H_{sand} = H\), then: \(H_{silt} = 2H\), \(H_{clay} = \dfrac{3}{2}(2H) = 3H\)
    Total thickness \(= H + 2H + 3H = 6H\)
  2. Calculate \(k_h\):
    \[k_h = \frac{(100k \cdot H) + (10k \cdot 2H) + (k \cdot 3H)}{6H} = \frac{100k + 20k + 3k}{6} = \frac{123k}{6} = 20.5k \]
  3. Calculate \(k_v\):
    \[k_v = \frac{6H}{\dfrac{H}{100k} + \dfrac{2H}{10k} + \dfrac{3H}{k}} = \frac{6H}{H\left(\dfrac{1 + 20 + 300}{100k}\right)} = \frac{6 \times 100k}{321} = \frac{600k}{321} = 1.869k \]
  4. Calculate the Ratio:
    \[\frac{k_h}{k_v} = \frac{20.5k}{1.869k} = 10.97 \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 10.97  |  Accepted key range: 10.0 to 12.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A square footing (2 m x 2 m) is subjected to an inclined point load, P as shown in the figure below. The water table is located well below the base of the footing. Considering one-way eccentricity, the net safe load carrying capacity of the footing for a factor of safety of 3.0 is __________ kN.

The following factors may be used:

Bearing capacity factors: \(N_q = 33.3, N_\gamma = 37.16\); Shape factors: \(F_{qs} = F_{\gamma s} = 1.314\); Depth factors: \(F_{qd} = F_{\gamma d} = 1.113\); Inclination factors: \(F_{qi} = 0.444, F_{\gamma i} = 0.02\)
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Foundation Engineering (Bearing Capacity)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Square footing: \(2\text{ m} \times 2\text{ m}\) (\(B = 2\text{ m}\), \(L = 2\text{ m}\))
    • Depth of embedment: \(D_f = 1\text{ m}\)
    • Eccentricity: Load applied at \(0.85\text{ m}\) from edge \(\implies e = 1.0 - 0.85 = 0.15\text{ m}\)
    • \(\gamma = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(c = 0\), \(\phi = 35^\circ\)
    • Load inclined at \(\alpha = 30^\circ\) to vertical
    • Bearing capacity, shape, depth, and inclination factors are provided.
    • Factor of Safety: \(\text{FOS} = 3.0\)
  • Aim: Determine the net safe load carrying capacity (kN).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Meyerhof's Effective Area Method: For eccentric loading, modified dimensions: \(B' = B - 2e\), \(L' = L\), \(A' = B' \times L'\)
  • Ultimate Bearing Capacity: \[q_u = \bar{q}\,N_q\,F_{qs}\,F_{qd}\,F_{qi} + \frac{1}{2}\gamma B'\,N_\gamma\,F_{\gamma s}\,F_{\gamma d}\,F_{\gamma i} \]
  • Net Safe Load: \[q_{nu} = q_u - \gamma D_f, \quad q_{ns} = \frac{q_{nu}}{\text{FOS}}, \quad Q_{ns} = q_{ns} \times A' \]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Effective Dimensions:
    \[B' = 2 - 2(0.15) = 1.7\text{ m}, \quad L' = 2\text{ m} \]\[A' = 1.7 \times 2 = 3.4\text{ m}^2 \]\[\bar{q} = \gamma D_f = 18 \times 1 = 18\text{ kPa} \]
  2. Calculate Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(q_u\)):
    • \(q\)-term: \(18 \times 33.3 \times 1.314 \times 1.113 \times 0.444 = 389.28\text{ kPa}\)
    • \(\gamma\)-term: \(0.5 \times 18 \times 1.7 \times 37.16 \times 1.314 \times 1.113 \times 0.02 = 16.63\text{ kPa}\)
    • \(q_u = 389.28 + 16.63 = 405.91\text{ kPa}\)
  3. Calculate Net Safe Vertical Load:
    \[q_{nu} = 405.91 - 18 = 387.91\text{ kPa} \]\[q_{ns} = \frac{387.91}{3} = 129.30\text{ kPa} \]\[Q_{ns} = 129.30 \times 3.4 = 439.63\text{ kN} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 439.63 kN  |  Accepted key range: 434 to 444

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: Two reservoirs are connected through a 930 m long, 0.3 m diameter pipe, which has a gate valve. The pipe entrance is sharp (loss coefficient = 0.5) and the valve is half-open (loss coefficient = 5.5). The head difference between the two reservoirs is 20 m. Assume the friction factor for the pipe as 0.03 and \(g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2\). The discharge in the pipe accounting for all minor and major losses is __________ m³/s.
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Pipe Flow

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Length: \(L = 930\text{ m}\), Diameter: \(D = 0.3\text{ m}\)
    • Head difference: \(H = 20\text{ m}\)
    • Friction factor: \(f = 0.03\), Gravity: \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)
    • Minor loss coefficients: Entrance \(K_{ent} = 0.5\), Valve \(K_{val} = 5.5\)
  • Aim: Compute the discharge \(Q\) in m³/s accounting for major and minor losses.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Apply Energy Conservation between two reservoirs.
  • Total head loss: \(H = h_{friction} + \sum h_{minor}\)
  • Minor losses include entrance, valve, and exit loss (standard exit loss \(K_{exit} = 1.0\)).
  • \[H = \left(\frac{fL}{D} + K_{ent} + K_{val} + K_{exit}\right)\frac{V^2}{2g} \]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up the Head Loss Equation:
    \[K_{total} = \frac{0.03 \times 930}{0.3} + 0.5 + 5.5 + 1.0 = 93 + 7 = 100 \]\[20 = 100 \times \frac{V^2}{2 \times 10} \implies 20 = 5V^2 \]
  2. Solve for Velocity:
    \[V^2 = \frac{20}{5} = 4 \implies V = 2\text{ m/s} \]
  3. Calculate Discharge:
    \[A = \frac{\pi}{4}(0.3)^2 = 0.070686\text{ m}^2 \]\[Q = A \times V = 0.070686 \times 2 = 0.14137\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.141 m³/s  |  Accepted key range: 0.140 to 0.142

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A hydraulic jump is formed in a 2 m wide rectangular channel which is horizontal and frictionless. The post-jump depth and velocity are 0.8 m and 1 m/s, respectively. The pre-jump velocity is __________ m/s. (use g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow (Hydraulic Jump)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Rectangular channel, width \(B = 2\text{ m}\), \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)
    • Post-jump variables: depth \(y_2 = 0.8\text{ m}\), velocity \(V_2 = 1\text{ m/s}\)
  • Aim: Find the pre-jump velocity \(V_1\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Unit Discharge Continuity: \(q = y_1 V_1 = y_2 V_2\)
  • Conjugate Depth Relationship for rectangular channel: \[y_1 = \frac{y_2}{2}\left(\sqrt{1 + 8\,Fr_2^2} - 1\right) \]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find unit discharge \(q\) and \(Fr_2^2\):
    \[q = y_2 V_2 = 0.8 \times 1 = 0.8\text{ m}^2/\text{s} \]\[Fr_2^2 = \frac{V_2^2}{g\,y_2} = \frac{1^2}{10 \times 0.8} = \frac{1}{8} = 0.125 \]
  2. Find pre-jump depth \(y_1\):
    \[y_1 = \frac{0.8}{2}\left(\sqrt{1 + 8(0.125)} - 1\right) = 0.4\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right) \]\[y_1 = 0.4 \times (1.4142 - 1) = 0.4 \times 0.4142 = 0.16568\text{ m} \]
  3. Calculate \(V_1\):
    \[V_1 = \frac{q}{y_1} = \frac{0.8}{0.16568} = 4.828\text{ m/s} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.83 m/s  |  Accepted key range: 4.75 to 4.85

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A short reach of a 2 m wide rectangular open channel has its bed level rising in the direction of flow at a slope of 1 in 10000. It carries a discharge of 4 m³/s and its Manning’s roughness coefficient is 0.01. The flow in this reach is gradually varying. At a certain section in this reach, the depth of flow was measured as 0.5 m. The rate of change of the water depth with distance, dy/dx, at this section is __________ (use g = 10 m/s²).
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow (Gradually Varied Flow)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Channel width: \(B = 2\text{ m}\)
    • Bed slope rises → \(S_0 = -1/10000 = -0.0001\) (negative: adverse slope)
    • Discharge: \(Q = 4\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\), Manning's \(n = 0.01\)
    • Measured depth: \(y = 0.5\text{ m}\), \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Determine the rate of change of depth \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • GVF Dynamic Equation: \[\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{S_0 - S_f}{1 - Fr^2} \]
  • Froude Number: \(Fr^2 = \dfrac{V^2}{g\,y}\)
  • Friction Slope (Manning's): \[S_f = \left(\frac{n\,Q}{A\,R^{2/3}}\right)^2 \]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Geometric Parameters:
    \[A = 2 \times 0.5 = 1.0\text{ m}^2, \quad P = 2 + 2(0.5) = 3.0\text{ m} \]\[R = \frac{1.0}{3.0} = 0.3333\text{ m} \implies R^{2/3} = 0.4807 \]
  2. Calculate Velocity and \(Fr^2\):
    \[V = \frac{Q}{A} = \frac{4}{1.0} = 4\text{ m/s} \]\[Fr^2 = \frac{4^2}{10 \times 0.5} = \frac{16}{5} = 3.2 \]
  3. Calculate Friction Slope (\(S_f\)):
    \[S_f = \left(\frac{0.01 \times 4}{1.0 \times 0.4807}\right)^2 = (0.08320)^2 = 0.006922 \]
  4. Determine \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\):
    \[\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{-0.0001 - 0.006922}{1 - 3.2} = \frac{-0.007022}{-2.2} = 0.003192 \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.00319  |  Accepted key range: 0.0031 to 0.0033

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: The drag force, \(F_D\), on a sphere kept in a uniform flow field depends on the diameter of the sphere, D; flow velocity, V; fluid density, \(\rho\); and dynamic viscosity, \(\mu\). Which of the following options represents the non-dimensional parameters which could be used to analyze this problem?
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Dimensional Analysis

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Application
  • Given Data: Variables — Drag force \(F_D\), diameter \(D\), velocity \(V\), density \(\rho\), dynamic viscosity \(\mu\).
  • Aim: Identify the correct non-dimensional parameters (Pi terms) matching the options.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Buckingham Pi Theorem:
    • Total variables: \(n = 5\) (\(F_D, D, V, \rho, \mu\))
    • Fundamental dimensions: \(m = 3\) (\(M, L, T\))
    • Number of \(\Pi\) terms \(= n - m = 5 - 3 = 2\)
  • Repeating variables selected: \(\rho, D, V\) (representing density, geometry, and kinematics).

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. First \(\Pi\) term (using \(F_D\)):
    Dimensions: \([F_D] = MLT^{-2}\), \([\rho] = ML^{-3}\), \([V] = LT^{-1}\), \([D] = L\)
    Standard drag coefficient formulation:
    \[\Pi_1 = \frac{F_D}{\rho V^2 D^2} \]
    Verification: \(\dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{(ML^{-3})(L^2T^{-2})(L^2)} = \dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{MLT^{-2}} = 1\) ✓
  2. Second \(\Pi\) term (using \(\mu\)):
    Dimensions: \([\mu] = ML^{-1}T^{-1}\)
    Standard Reynolds Number formulation:
    \[\Pi_2 = \frac{\rho V D}{\mu} \]
    Verification: \(\dfrac{(ML^{-3})(LT^{-1})(L)}{ML^{-1}T^{-1}} = \dfrac{ML^{-1}T^{-1}}{ML^{-1}T^{-1}} = 1\) ✓
  3. Check given Options:
    Option (C) matches perfectly: \(\dfrac{F_D}{\rho V^2 D^2}\) and \(\dfrac{\rho V D}{\mu}\)

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Option (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: In a catchment, there are four rain-gauge stations, P, Q, R, and S. Normal annual precipitation values at these stations are 780 mm, 850 mm, 920 mm, and 980 mm, respectively. In the year 2013, stations Q, R, and S, were operative but P was not. Using the normal ratio method, the precipitation at station P for the year 2013 has been estimated as 860 mm. If the observed precipitation at stations Q and R for the year 2013 were 930 mm and 1010 mm, respectively; what was the observed precipitation (in mm) at station S for that year?
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Precipitation & Missing Data Estimation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    StationNormal Annual Precipitation (mm)Observed 2013 Precipitation (mm)
    P (missing)\(N_P = 780\)\(P_P = 860\) (estimated)
    Q\(N_Q = 850\)\(P_Q = 930\)
    R\(N_R = 920\)\(P_R = 1010\)
    S\(N_S = 980\)\(P_S = ?\)
  • Aim: Find the observed precipitation at station S (\(P_S\)) for 2013.

3. Core Concepts:

Normal Ratio Method: When the normal annual precipitation of index stations differs by more than 10% from the missing station, the Normal Ratio Method is used: \[P_P = \frac{N_P}{m}\left(\frac{P_Q}{N_Q} + \frac{P_R}{N_R} + \frac{P_S}{N_S}\right) \] where \(m = 3\) is the number of index stations.

4. Solution Method:

Substitute known values into the Normal Ratio Method formula and solve linearly for \(P_S\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Setup the equation:
    \[860 = \frac{780}{3}\left(\frac{930}{850} + \frac{1010}{920} + \frac{P_S}{980}\right) \]
  2. Simplify constants:
    \[860 = 260\left(1.09412 + 1.09783 + \frac{P_S}{980}\right) \]
  3. Isolate the bracket:
    \[\frac{860}{260} = 2.19195 + \frac{P_S}{980} \]\[3.30769 = 2.19195 + \frac{P_S}{980} \]
  4. Solve for \(P_S\):
    \[\frac{P_S}{980} = 3.30769 - 2.19195 = 1.11574 \]\[P_S = 1.11574 \times 980 = 1093.43\text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1093.43 mm  |  Accepted key range: 1093 to 1094

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
The 4-hr unit hydrograph for a catchment is given in the table below. What would be the maximum ordinate of the S-curve (in m³/s) derived from this hydrograph?

Time (hr)024681012141618202224
Unit hydrograph ordinate (m³/s)00.63.110139520.70.30.20.10
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Hydrographs & S-Curve

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Duration of Unit Hydrograph (UH) = 4 hours; ordinates of 4-hr UH provided at 2-hour intervals.
  • Aim: Determine the maximum ordinate of the resulting S-curve.

3. Core Concepts:

An S-curve represents the hydrograph produced by continuous effective rainfall at a constant rate for an indefinite period. questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
The concentration of Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂) in ambient atmosphere was measured as 30 \(\mu\)g/m³. Under the same conditions, the above SO₂ concentration expressed in ppm is __________.

Given: \(P/(RT) = 41.6 \text{ mol/m}^3\); where, P = Pressure; T = Temperature; R = universal gas constant; Molecular weight of SO₂ = 64.
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Air Pollution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Concentration of \(SO_2 = 30\,\mu\text{g/m}^3\)
    • \(P/(RT) = 41.6\text{ mol/m}^3\)
    • Molecular weight of \(SO_2 = 64\text{ g/mol}\)
  • Aim: Express the concentration in parts per million (ppm) by volume.

3. Core Concepts:

By the Ideal Gas Law (\(PV = nRT\)), \(P/(RT)\) represents the total molar density of air (\(n/V\)). The concentration of a gaseous pollutant in ppmv is its mole fraction multiplied by \(10^6\): \[\text{ppm} = \left(\frac{\text{Moles of Pollutant}}{\text{Total Moles of Air}}\right) \times 10^6 \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Find the mass of \(SO_2\) in \(1\text{ m}^3\) of air.
  2. Convert that mass into moles of \(SO_2\).
  3. Divide by the total moles of air in \(1\text{ m}^3\) (given by \(P/RT\)).
  4. Multiply by \(10^6\) to get ppm.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Mass of \(SO_2\) in \(1\text{ m}^3\):
    \[m = 30\,\mu\text{g} = 30 \times 10^{-6}\text{ g} \]
  2. Moles of \(SO_2\) in \(1\text{ m}^3\):
    \[n_{SO_2} = \frac{30 \times 10^{-6}}{64} = 4.6875 \times 10^{-7}\text{ mol} \]
  3. Total moles of air per m³:
    \[n_{\text{air}} = \frac{P}{RT} = 41.6\text{ mol} \]
  4. Calculate ppm:
    \[\text{ppm} = \frac{4.6875 \times 10^{-7}}{41.6} \times 10^6 = 1.1268 \times 10^{-8} \times 10^6 = 0.011268 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.011 ppm  |  Accepted key range: 0.010 to 0.012

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q60
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
Consider a primary sedimentation tank (PST) in a water treatment plant with Surface Overflow Rate (SOR) of 40 m³/m²/d. The diameter of the spherical particle which will have 90 percent theoretical removal efficiency in this tank is __________ \(\mu\)m. Assume that settling velocity of the particles in water is described by Stokes’s Law.

Given: Density of water = 1000 kg/m³; Density of particle = 2650 kg/m³; g = 9.81 m/s²; Kinematic viscosity of water (v) = \(1.10 \times 10^{-6}\) m²/s
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment (Sedimentation)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Surface Overflow Rate (SOR): \(v_o = 40\text{ m}^3/\text{m}^2/\text{d}\)
    • Theoretical removal efficiency: \(\eta = 90\%\)
    • Density of water: \(\rho_w = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3\)
    • Density of particle: \(\rho_p = 2650\text{ kg/m}^3\)
    • Kinematic viscosity: \(\nu = 1.10 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}\)
    • Gravity: \(g = 9.81\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Calculate the diameter of the spherical particle (\(d\)) in \(\mu\text{m}\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Removal Efficiency: \(\eta = \dfrac{v_s}{v_o}\), where \(v_s\) is the settling velocity and \(v_o\) is the SOR.
  • Stokes's Law: \[v_s = \frac{g(\rho_p - \rho_w)d^2}{18\mu} = \frac{g\left(\dfrac{\rho_p}{\rho_w}-1\right)d^2}{18\nu} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert SOR (\(v_o\)) to m/s.
  2. Calculate required settling velocity (\(v_s\)) using efficiency.
  3. Apply Stokes's law and solve for \(d\).
  4. Convert \(d\) from meters to \(\mu\text{m}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Convert \(v_o\):
    \[v_o = \frac{40}{24 \times 3600} = 4.6296 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m/s} \]
  2. Calculate Settling Velocity (\(v_s\)):
    \[v_s = 0.90 \times 4.6296 \times 10^{-4} = 4.1667 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m/s} \]
  3. Apply Stokes's Law to find \(d^2\):
    \[4.1667 \times 10^{-4} = \frac{9.81 \times (2.65 - 1) \times d^2}{18 \times 1.10 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{9.81 \times 1.65 \times d^2}{19.8 \times 10^{-6}} \]\[4.1667 \times 10^{-4} = 817500 \cdot d^2 \]\[d^2 = \frac{4.1667 \times 10^{-4}}{817500} = 5.0968 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}^2 \]
  4. Solve for \(d\):
    \[d = \sqrt{5.0968 \times 10^{-10}} = 2.2576 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m} = 22.576\,\mu\text{m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 22.58 μm  |  Accepted key range: 20.0 to 24.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q61
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
The acceleration-time relationship for a vehicle subjected to non-uniform acceleration is,

\[\frac{dv}{dt} = (\alpha - \beta v_0)e^{-\beta t} \]

where, \(v\) is the speed in m/s, \(t\) is the time in s, \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are parameters, and \(v_0\) is the initial speed in m/s. If the accelerating behavior of a vehicle, whose driver intends to overtake a slow moving vehicle ahead, is described as,

\[\frac{dv}{dt} = (\alpha - \beta v) \]

Considering \(\alpha = 2 \text{ m/s}^2\), \(\beta = 0.05 \text{ s}^{-1}\) and \(\frac{dv}{dt} = 1.3 \text{ m/s}^2\) at \(t = 3\) s, the distance (in m) travelled by the vehicle in 35 s is __________.
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Traffic Engineering (Vehicle Kinematics)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Acceleration: \(a(t) = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = (\alpha - \beta v_0)e^{-\beta t}\)
    • Parameters: \(\alpha = 2\text{ m/s}^2\), \(\beta = 0.05\text{ s}^{-1}\)
    • Condition: at \(t = 3\text{ s}\), \(a = 1.3\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Calculate the distance travelled (\(S\)) in 35 seconds.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Velocity is the integral of acceleration: \(v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt + v_0\)
  • Distance is the integral of velocity: \(S(t) = \int v(t)\,dt\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Find initial velocity (\(v_0\)) from the condition at \(t = 3\text{ s}\).
  2. Integrate \(a(t)\) to derive velocity function \(v(t)\).
  3. Integrate \(v(t)\) from \(0\) to \(35\text{ s}\) to find total distance.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find \(v_0\):
    \[(2 - 0.05v_0)e^{-0.05 \times 3} = 1.3 \]\[2 - 0.05v_0 = 1.3 \times e^{0.15} \approx 1.3 \times 1.16183 = 1.51038 \]\[v_0 = \frac{2 - 1.51038}{0.05} = 9.7924\text{ m/s} \]
  2. Formulate Velocity Function \(v(t)\):
    \[v(t) = \int(\alpha - \beta v_0)e^{-\beta t}\,dt = \frac{\alpha}{\beta} - \left(\frac{\alpha}{\beta} - v_0\right)e^{-\beta t} \]
    With \(\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta} = \dfrac{2}{0.05} = 40\):
    \[v(t) = 40 - (40 - 9.7924)e^{-0.05t} = 40 - 30.2076\,e^{-0.05t} \]
  3. Calculate Distance in 35 s:
    \[S(35) = \int_0^{35}\left(40 - 30.2076\,e^{-0.05t}\right)dt \]\[ S(35) = \left[40t + \frac{30.2076}{0.05}e^{-0.05t}\right]_0^{35} = \left[40t + 604.152\,e^{-0.05t}\right]_0^{35} \]\[S(35) = (1400 + 604.152 \times 0.17377) - (0 + 604.152) \]\[S(35) = 1400 + 104.985 - 604.152 = 900.83\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 900.83 m  |  Accepted key range: 895 to 905

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q62
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: On a circular curve, the rate of superelevation is \(e\). While negotiating the curve a vehicle comes to a stop. It is seen that the stopped vehicle does not slide inwards (in the radial direction). The coefficient of side friction is \(f\). Which of the following is true:
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Geometric Design (Horizontal Curves)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Superelevation rate: \(e\)
    • Stopped vehicle (\(v = 0\)) does not slide inwards
    • Coefficient of lateral friction: \(f\)
  • Aim: Identify the correct relationship between \(e\) and \(f\).

3. Core Concepts:

When a vehicle halts on a superelevated curve (banked at angle \(\theta\)), the centrifugal force is zero. Forces parallel to the road surface are:

  • Gravity component pulling inwards: \(W\sin\theta\)
  • Resisting friction acting outwards: \(fN = fW\cos\theta\)

For the vehicle not to slide inwards: Inward Force \(\leq\) Outward Friction Capacity.

4. Solution Method:

Set up the no-sliding inequality:

\[W\sin\theta \leq fW\cos\theta \implies \tan\theta \leq f \]

Since rate of superelevation \(e = \tan\theta\):

\[e \leq f \]

5. Final Answer:

Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q63
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: A sign is required to be put up asking drivers to slow down to 30 km/h before entering Zone Y (see figure). On this road, vehicles require 174 m to slow down to 30 km/h (the distance of 174 m includes the distance travelled during the perception-reaction time of drivers). The sign can be read by 6/6 vision drivers from a distance of 48 m. The sign is placed at a distance of x m from the start of Zone Y so that even a 6/9 vision driver can slow down to 30 km/h before entering the zone. The minimum value of x is __________ m.
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Geometric Design (Sight Distance)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Distance to slow down to \(30\text{ km/h}\) (includes PIEV time) = \(174\text{ m}\)
    • 6/6 vision reading distance = \(48\text{ m}\)
    • Design driver has 6/9 vision
  • Aim: Find the minimum placement distance (\(x\)) of the sign from Zone Y.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Visual Acuity (Snellen Fraction): A person with 6/9 vision needs to be at \(6\text{ m}\) to read what a normal 6/6 person reads at \(9\text{ m}\).
  • Visual Acuity Ratio \(= \dfrac{6/9}{6/6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\)
  • Reading distance for 6/9 driver: \(D_{6/9} = D_{6/6} \times \dfrac{2}{3}\)
  • The total distance from where the sign is read to Zone Y must be \(\geq\) the required slowing distance.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute the reading distance for a 6/9 vision driver.
  2. Set the sum of the reading distance and sign placement distance (\(x\)) equal to the required slowing distance.
  3. Solve for \(x\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Reading Distance for 6/9 driver:
    \[D_{6/9} = 48 \times \frac{2}{3} = 32\text{ m} \]
  2. Equate Distances:
    Total available slowing distance = \(x\) (sign to Zone Y) + \(32\text{ m}\) (sign reading distance)
    \[x + 32 \geq 174 \implies x = 174 - 32 = 142\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 142 m  |  Accepted key range: 141.84 to 142.32

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q64
questions.subject: Surveying & Geomatics
questions.question: In a survey work, three independent angles X, Y and Z were observed with weights \(W_X, W_Y, W_Z\), respectively. The weight of the sum of angles X, Y and Z is given by:
questions.explanation:
Surveying | Theory of Errors

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Independent angles \(X, Y, Z\) with weights \(W_X, W_Y, W_Z\).
  • Aim: Determine the weight of their sum \((X + Y + Z)\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Error Propagation for independent quantities: Variance of a sum equals the sum of individual variances: \[\sigma_S^2 = \sigma_X^2 + \sigma_Y^2 + \sigma_Z^2 \]
  • Weight-Variance relationship: \(W \propto \dfrac{1}{\sigma^2} \implies \sigma^2 \propto \dfrac{1}{W}\)

4. Solution Method:

Substitute the inverse weight relationship into the variance equation:

\[\frac{1}{W_S} = \frac{1}{W_X} + \frac{1}{W_Y} + \frac{1}{W_Z} \]

Taking the reciprocal:

\[W_S = \frac{1}{\dfrac{1}{W_X} + \dfrac{1}{W_Y} + \dfrac{1}{W_Z}} \]

5. Final Answer:

Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q65
questions.subject: Surveying & Geomatics
questions.question: In a region with magnetic declination of 2°E, the magnetic Fore bearing (FB) of a line AB was measured as N79°50'E. There was local attraction at A. To determine the correct magnetic bearing of the line, a point O was selected at which there was no local attraction. The magnetic FB of line AO and OA were observed to be S52°40'E and N50°20'W, respectively. What is the true FB of line AB?
questions.explanation:
Surveying | Compass Surveying & Local Attraction

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Declination = \(2^\circ\text{ E}\)
    • Measured Magnetic FB of \(AB\) = \(N\,79^\circ 50'\,E\)
    • Local attraction exists at \(A\); Point \(O\) is free from local attraction
    • Measured Magnetic FB of \(AO\) = \(S\,52^\circ 40'\,E\)
    • Measured Magnetic FB of \(OA\) = \(N\,50^\circ 20'\,W\)
  • Aim: Determine the True Fore Bearing (FB) of line \(AB\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • The station free from local attraction yields correct bearings.
  • Back Bearing (BB) = Fore Bearing (FB) \(\pm 180^\circ\) (or reversed quadrants: N \(\leftrightarrow\) S, E \(\leftrightarrow\) W).
  • Correction at station = Correct Bearing − Observed Bearing.
  • True Bearing = Corrected Magnetic Bearing + Declination (East is positive).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Since \(O\) is free from local attraction, the measured FB of \(OA\) is correct.
  2. Deduce the correct BB of \(OA\), which is the correct FB of \(AO\).
  3. Compare correct FB of \(AO\) with the observed FB of \(AO\) at \(A\) to find the local attraction correction.
  4. Apply correction to the observed FB of \(AB\) to get the corrected magnetic bearing of \(AB\).
  5. Apply magnetic declination to find True Bearing.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Correct Bearings based on station O:
    Observed (correct) FB of \(OA = N\,50^\circ 20'\,W\)
    Correct FB of \(AO\) (BB of \(OA\)) = \(S\,50^\circ 20'\,E\)
  2. Calculate correction at A (using WCB):
    • Correct FB of \(AO\) in WCB \(= 180^\circ - 50^\circ 20' = 129^\circ 40'\)
    • Observed FB of \(AO\) in WCB \(= 180^\circ - 52^\circ 40' = 127^\circ 20'\)
    • Correction at \(A = 129^\circ 40' - 127^\circ 20' = +2^\circ 20'\)
  3. Correct Magnetic Bearing of AB:
    Observed FB of \(AB\) in WCB \(= 79^\circ 50'\)
    \[\text{Corrected Mag. FB of } AB = 79^\circ 50' + 2^\circ 20' = 82^\circ 10' \quad (N\,82^\circ 10'\,E) \]
  4. Convert to True Bearing:
    \[\text{True FB of } AB = 82^\circ 10' + 2^\circ 00' = 84^\circ 10' \quad (N\,84^\circ 10'\,E) \]

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (C)
